Identify Significant Components via RMT and Inter-block Coherence Tests

Source: R/utils.R
significant_components.Rd

Assess declared supplied-noise spectral edges and optional common-feature loading coherence. Arbitrary multiblock loadings are not assumed to share a feature space, and an asymptotic support edge is not a calibrated p-value.

Usage

significant_components(
  fit,
  n,
  k_vec = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  check_rmt = TRUE,
  tail_frac = 0.3,
  noise_variance = NULL,
  spectrum = c("unknown", "covariance", "singular"),
  noise_model = c("unknown", "isotropic"),
  n_eff = n,
  check_icc = FALSE,
  common_features = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted multi-block model object containing at minimum a `V_list` attribute (list of loading matrices) and optionally `sdev` (singular values).

n

Integer; the number of observations (rows) used to fit the model.

k_vec

Optional integer vector of block dimensions (number of columns per original data block). If NULL, inferred from loading-matrix row counts. Supplied counts and block-index metadata must agree with those fitted feature counts, including any preprocessing that changes the feature dimension.

alpha

Finite probability strictly between 0 and 1; the threshold for explicitly enabled experimental ICC (default 0.05). Explicit alpha without ICC warns that it is inapplicable; an MP support edge is not alpha-level.

check_rmt

Logical; if TRUE (default), performs the Marchenko-Pastur edge test to check if eigenvalues exceed the noise threshold.

tail_frac

Retained for compatibility. Automatic noise estimation from truncated fitted spectra is unavailable; this argument does not estimate noise.

noise_variance

Positive finite noise variance, supplied independently in covariance-eigenvalue units. No automatic estimate is assumed.

spectrum

Spectral units: `"covariance"` means `sdev^2` are covariance eigenvalues; `"singular"` means raw singular values, divided by `n_eff` after squaring. The default `"unknown"` leaves RMT unavailable.

noise_model

`"isotropic"` explicitly declares the IID isotropic noise model. The default `"unknown"` leaves RMT unavailable, including for arbitrary weighted MFA compromise spectra.

n_eff

Positive effective degrees of freedom of the covariance normalization, at most `n`; defaults to `n` for an uncentered model. For a centered unweighted sample covariance, supply `n - 1`.

check_icc

Logical; explicitly request the experimental common-feature coherence criterion (default FALSE). It is independent of RMT applicability.

common_features

Unique character feature identities declaring a common coordinate domain for ICC. Every loading matrix must have exactly these row identities; rows are matched by identity before comparison. Equal widths alone do not establish a common space.

Value

A list with the following elements:

keep

Component indices passing all enabled criteria. A requested unavailable criterion cannot retain components. With both disabled, no components are declared retained.

rmt_pass

Logical edge decisions, or NA if RMT is unavailable/disabled.

icc_pass

Experimental ICC decisions, or NA when disabled.

icc

Numeric vector of inter-block coherence values per component.

icc_pvalue

Numeric vector of p-values for the ICC test.

mp_edge

The Marchenko-Pastur edge threshold (NA if RMT skipped).

sigma2_est

Supplied noise variance (legacy field name; NA if unavailable).

lambda

Eigenvalues (squared singular values).

n, k_vec, alpha

Input parameters echoed back.

rmt_status, rmt_reason

Whether the requested edge was evaluated, unavailable, or explicitly disabled, and why. Unavailable is never a pass.

gamma, n_eff, spectrum, noise_model

Resolved aspect ratio and declared units/model.

icc_status

`"disabled"` or `"evaluated_experimental"`.

Details

The supplied-noise RMT criterion uses the asymptotic Marchenko-Pastur upper support edge. This is not an alpha-level finite-sample significance test. Its isotropic covariance representation must be declared explicitly; no noise variance is inferred from a few retained fitted components.

The ICC test measures the squared cosine similarity of loading vectors across pairs of explicitly matched common-feature blocks. Its Gaussian null approximation with Bonferroni correction remains experimental; feature-domain validation does not establish statistical calibration.
